scope: Exactly the last 54 investigated holds; no new discovery. Ten newer company records reconciled separately using main-reviewed evidence.
method: Re-read every prior substantive assessment; reuse detailed primary captures and browser investigations, with targeted new product/case/career/alias reads. Not a claim of 54 newly fetched sites. Each remaining hold states a specific unresolved fact, not an unfetched placeholder.
activityLimit: Original technology, present activity, identity and local occupancy are distinct. Quiet startups and failed individual pages are not inactivity findings.
consys: Main independently approved the recommendation; exact operation staged disabled. ITIVITY remains unapproved.

rows.name: Stutz Medien AG
rows.reason: Digital Unit, explicitly Stutz's offering, maintains Gaia Core as a common headless platform across several product tiers and implementations, with extension, intelligence and care modules. This is concrete reusable maintained software, not a requirement to invent the underlying CMS. Sanity remains the upstream CMS; its native collaboration features are not credited as Stutz inventions.

rows.name: Accenture Switzerland
rows.reason: Zurich Innovation Hub and Liquid Studio primary material establishes local prototype/application engineering; named global products do not identify the Swiss team's contribution. Remaining question: which maintained original technology or product-development programme belongs to this local operation? Neither generic consulting work nor the global brand settles that question.

rows.name: AutoMate Insurance AG
rows.reason: The fully rendered executive-solutions page establishes a concrete branded insurance platform, calculators and processing, not an access failure. Remaining question: does AutoMate develop this platform or distribute another software provider's system? Developer attribution, not patent ownership, would resolve this.

rows.name: Beriflapp
rows.reason: Product-innovation and FinSat evidence establishes original client delivery, but CityL3ns is explicitly FinSat's product. Remaining question: does Beriflapp maintain a reusable technology of its own beyond these commissioned deliveries? Do not assign FinSat's product to its contractor; no IP certificate is required.

rows.name: Blackpoints
rows.reason: The recovered catalogue attributes GIPE to CAMAC integration and identifies Inventsys/iGovPortal as partners. Remaining question: is there a named original maintained Blackpoints component or substantive upstream contribution beyond client forms and integration? The published named examples do not establish that attribution.

rows.name: Comerge
rows.reason: The current official CoffeeRace case attributes the original idea, project management and software development to Comerge, establishing its own concrete application rather than borrowing a client brand. Failure to retrieve CoffeeRace's separate site is not evidence that Comerge stopped developing technology. Separate live-service availability has not been verified; Connect is not treated as Comerge-owned.

rows.name: cross-works
rows.reason: KIM's product page contains conflicting developer/hosting attribution: Swiss operator language alongside development and servers in Ravensburg. Exact-name primary-page checks did not resolve the supplier identity. Remaining question: is CrossWorks the developer or the Swiss reseller/operator of KIM? Do not treat reused supplier text as proof of original development.

rows.name: Cyberlink
rows.reason: Recommend exclusion, pending main review: the detailed OpenStack and VPC offerings explicitly supply cloudscale and VMware platforms; the Semax case supplies connectivity rather than developing Semax technology. Across inspected products and case work the affirmative business is managed infrastructure/connectivity. This does not deny engineering competence or disqualify all OSS use; it distinguishes the documented vendor-service offering from original technology.
rows.currentReason: Withdraw the exclusion recommendation: the current official support page explicitly attributes a from-scratch rebuild of its customer portal, with live service management, tickets, requests and billing. Concrete original maintained software is supported. VMware, cloudscale and Anapaya remain upstream vendors; no invention of their technology is inferred.

rows.name: Data Purpose
rows.reason: Recommend exclusion, pending main review: the full priced catalogue offers SAP/Microsoft architecture checks, roadmaps, proofs of concept, dashboard templates, coaching and support. The founders' account confirms implementation consultancy. Templates alone do not turn this positively documented client-service catalogue into an original maintained technology platform.

rows.name: Deloitte Zurich
rows.reason: Deloitte Switzerland's CEO explicitly describes in-house development of Solaria in the spring-2026 interview and internal platform development in autumn 2025. This resolves the earlier Swiss attribution gap with a maintained AI application platform, not a global-product assumption. It does not establish that Deloitte developed the underlying foundation models.

rows.name: Digital Assets Technologies
rows.reason: The detailed Balance Report offering describes a concrete automated chain-snapshot/report pipeline with supply exclusions, immutable integrity records and PDF/JSON output. This branded maintained technical service is sufficient product evidence beyond generic crypto advice. NautBeacon is a named component, not separately claimed as the company's invention.

rows.name: ECOPARTS
rows.reason: The tooling page establishes manufacture and adaptation of cooled sprue bushes using laser sintering; the original standard designs came from MoldMasters. Remaining question: is the changed manufacturing process an original developed process or standard additive manufacture of supplied designs? Technical production is real; neither MoldMasters' invention nor a proprietary-process claim can be assumed.

rows.name: ETAVIS
rows.reason: The Safety Lock article proves in-house design and repeat manufacture, not resale. The remaining issue is scope: development is explicitly in Basel and the output is a simple mechanical lockout accessory. Main must decide whether that group-level product qualifies this Zurich listing, or identify a relevant local development programme. No further patent or ownership documentation is required.

rows.name: evolyze GmbH
rows.reason: The company and client material identifies genuine software/data engineering and Vatorex's MVP. Remaining question: what original technology does Evolyze maintain beyond customer-only delivery? Do not attribute the customer's product to Evolyze, but do not infer inactivity or lack of technical competence.

rows.name: fahrenheit
rows.reason: The STMZ case explicitly documents an original PHP platform maintained over many years and a REST API built from scratch for the newly released 2025 app. Together with the company's original platform concept, this is concrete maintained software, not generic site configuration. STMZ remains the customer and brand; no exclusive-rights or patent claim is made.

rows.name: Forte Digital
rows.reason: The current office list names locations outside Switzerland and the work examples are client platforms. Remaining questions: is the listed Swiss operation still present, and does it maintain an original platform rather than only deliver client projects? Office-list omission does not prove closure; reconcile identity before any map action.

rows.name: Helvetic IT Solution
rows.reason: Recommend exclusion, pending main review: the inspected service catalogue affirmatively sells support, vendor cloud/backup and commissioned websites/software. Its public marketing calculators are not a substantive technology product. This is a service-catalogue decision, not an exclusion for sparse publicity or a failed fetch.

rows.name: icentic
rows.reason: Incubation and founder overlap with beppo are explicit, but neither establishes that the listed icentic entity develops the beppo platform. Remaining question: what is the actual product-development/entity relationship, or another named original maintained icentic technology? Do not silently transfer founder or sister-company products.

rows.name: incendia
rows.reason: Recommend exclusion, pending main review: the detailed catalogue expressly starts with SAP standard functionality and delivers customer extensions, interfaces, forms, applications and support. This is affirmative client-only implementation work. SAP is not Incendia's technology; no original separate product or maintained common component is claimed in the inspected offering.

rows.name: Joylab
rows.reason: Named projects demonstrate original electronics and firmware engineering, including commissioned Seervision hardware, not mere consulting slogans. Remaining question is whether an original Joylab technology persists beyond the customer's deliverable. Customer robotics products must not be reassigned to Joylab; exclusive IP paperwork is not required to establish an identifiable reusable design.

rows.name: KOCH IT
rows.reason: Adnovum explicitly confirms the April-2026 absorption merger and incorporation into its public-sector team. Resolve the historical Koch identity and Winterthur occupancy against the existing Adnovum record. This is an identity/location question, not evidence of failed technology or a closed office.

rows.name: Linked Engineering
rows.reason: Detailed offering establishes original assembly design, contract engineering staff and production to customer specifications. Remaining question: which identifiable assembly/control technology does the company continue developing beyond customer-only design delivery? Do not require patents or exclude substantial engineering merely because it is commissioned.

rows.name: Mathys Partner
rows.reason: The detailed glare methodology establishes specialist simulation methods, but does not identify the simulator developer. Remaining question: does Mathys develop the calculation engine or a substantive original method, or operate licensed tools? The method's specificity is a real exception to generic consulting, not a reason to presume ownership.

rows.name: mecas
rows.reason: Current primary site describes a physical-AI lab and research collaborators; terms describe customer staffing, consulting and software services. Remaining question: what specific original model, system or research output is developed by this entity? The targeted primary search still provides no attributable artifact; young/private research status is not exclusion evidence.

rows.name: Microbe Investigations Switzerland
rows.reason: Testing catalogue and company history establish standard and tailored microbiological testing and a research background. Remaining question: is there an identifiable original assay, testing system or research method developed by MIS rather than standard-contract testing? Targeted research did not settle this; do not substitute founder history or a different similarly named laboratory.

rows.name: mp technology
rows.reason: The May-2026 festival-suite account attributes the original application and scheduling engine to MP technology and documents expansion into a reusable modular suite across festivals since 2024. Concrete continuing platform engineering resolves the earlier overstrict contractual-rights hold. The band association remains the commissioning customer; no exclusive IP claim is made.

rows.name: Nomasis
rows.reason: Recommend exclusion, pending main review: the current catalogue/history and previously inspected engineering-role duties consistently describe vendor MDM/MTD configuration, rollout, customer security and operation. These affirmatively establish managed mobile-IT services; generic research claims do not identify a separate original product. Do not count vendor platforms as Nomasis inventions.

rows.name: Novita Engineering
rows.reason: The engineering and production pages substantiate industrial design, procurement and manufacturing coordination, including sophisticated sectors. Remaining question: which concrete original machine, control system or process is maintained by Novita beyond customer-specific design delivery? Sector names and technical capability alone do not settle that product question.

rows.name: novu
rows.reason: The app catalogue identifies substantive Roots, Working Bicycle and hardware-interface development, but these are expressly client products. Remaining question: is Novu's internal app-distribution platform or another maintained component original Novu technology? Do not demand legal IP certificates, attribute the clients' businesses to Novu, or treat its acquisition as closure.

rows.name: onmit
rows.reason: Teacher Switch is genuine developed matching software but explicitly belongs to a separate startup; other catalogue entries are Microsoft services. Remaining question: does onmit maintain an original common platform/component beyond customer-specific delivery? This is technical attribution, not a patent requirement.

rows.name: Plat4mation
rows.reason: Current Move4U and partner-app pages establish continuing co-development, while the former 4Industry/4Facility business was divested. Remaining question: which currently maintained original application belongs to the represented Plat4mation operation, rather than the customer or divested entity? Historical innovation and client delivery must not silently substitute for that identity check.

rows.name: Pront
rows.reason: Recommend exclusion, pending main review: the detailed current cases describe Interdiscount cloud migration/DevOps/security and Helsana strategy, architecture and operating model. Together with its explicit consulting-boutique catalogue these affirmatively establish customer consulting/integration, not development of Helsana's own health platform by Pront.

rows.name: Quantum Digital
rows.reason: Named SelfService and MediaLink examples are customer projects; PIM/DAM offerings identify partners. Remaining question: what original maintained component is developed by Quantum Digital rather than supplied by those customers/vendors? The named technical exceptions warrant attribution, not an agency-label exclusion.

rows.name: Qubrix
rows.reason: Primary pages specifically describe solvers, reduced-order models, GPU/HPC development and licensing, but no identifiable current solver/model is attributed. Remaining question: name an original maintained or licensable technical artifact. Young-company sparse disclosure is not inactivity, and patents are unnecessary.

rows.name: Reasoning Labs
rows.reason: Current official page still states only a superintelligence aspiration and Reasoning Machines Inc identity. Earlier primary script/page investigation and the fresh page read provide no named research output or local-entity link. Remaining questions are the entity relationship and a concrete technical programme; this is not an exclusion for a quiet startup.

rows.name: relyz
rows.reason: Recommend exclusion, pending main review: the full engineering page describes customer strategy, websites/shops, portals, language-model integration, marketing automation and launch services. Its selected case is an IWP content hub and CRM introduction. The AI Discovery Lab language does not change this affirmative client-agency offering into a documented own technology platform.

rows.name: SCANVISION
rows.reason: The project catalogue and founders' account substantiate original interactive spatial visualisations and sensor interfaces. Remaining question: what maintained original renderer/interface or scientific method persists beyond the commissioned visualisations? Concrete development is recognised; no exclusive ownership proof or patent is required.

rows.name: Scheuss & Partner
rows.reason: The marketplace is a real SaaS provisioning/reporting/billing portal, not an unfetched hypothetical product. Its public application shell and product description do not identify the developer. Remaining question: does Scheuss develop a maintained original part of this portal or operate licensed tooling? Keep this specific exception open rather than infer ownership from branding.

rows.name: Sotronik
rows.reason: Primary material attributes SICOS hardware to Sulzer; the Kueng/IQONICS case establishes original commissioned controller firmware. Remaining question: does Sotronik maintain its own controller/software platform beyond this customer's design? Do not require patents or falsely credit SICOS manufacturing to Sotronik.

rows.name: STEP-X
rows.reason: The rendered catalogue credits ENOVIA/Scribe to vendors but does not identify the developer of ZOE Professional. Exact-name checks did not settle the author. Remaining question: is ZOE developed by Step-X or distributed? A primary developer attribution suffices; no IP certificate is required.

rows.name: Sunrise
rows.reason: The current official IT careers page identifies Wilmaa as Sunrise's OTT division and its software-engineering team as developing yallo TV, Wilmaa TV and MySports. This is direct maintained original product development, resolving the earlier network-operator-only uncertainty.

rows.name: Swiss Engineering Partners
rows.reason: The Make and Pack case proves original robotics/computer-vision engineering and a complete working prototype for Gategroup. Remaining question: is there a continuing company-developed robotics stack/platform beyond the commissioned system? Do not treat technical competence as missing, require patents, or rebrand Gategroup's system as an independently marketed SEP product.

rows.name: Swiss Infosec
rows.reason: Recommend exclusion of this consultancy listing, pending main review: its own GRC Toolbox page explicitly assigns software and operation to Swiss GRC, while Swiss Infosec supplies consulting and implementation. The sister-company relationship is real but cannot substitute for development by this listed entity. Preserve all records and do not automatically merge group identities.

rows.name: Swiss Robotics & Advanced Technologies
rows.reason: The inspected home and solutions pages combine autonomous/aerial-robot claims with integration/customisation services but identify no specific original robot or software system. Remaining question: what demonstrable technical design/programme does this entity develop? Sparse publicity is not a reason to classify it as inactive or generic-only.

rows.name: Synerma
rows.reason: The detailed current company catalogue distinguishes its automation platform from software brokerage and individual client products, and describes an extensively deployed COVID software platform. This is attributable continuing platform development beyond simple resale. SolarChain/Eventon/BTC remain client examples, not claimed Synerma-owned brands.

rows.name: tailorfast
rows.reason: The current offering and founder history establish specialised order-processing software, integrations and several demonstrations. Remaining question: is there a common original maintained order-processing engine, rather than only separately commissioned workflows? Do not demand legal title documents; product architecture/developer attribution would suffice.

rows.name: TekkMinds
rows.reason: The detailed case proves substantial original simulation software and five years of maintenance, using QEMU for an automotive customer. Remaining question: is the simulator a continuing TekkMinds technology or solely the customer's commissioned platform? QEMU integration alone is not disqualifying; neither customer scale nor contract maintenance automatically establishes an own product.

rows.name: TIMETOACT GROUP Schweiz
rows.reason: The Swiss site's detailed rapID page explicitly attributes development to TIMETOACT experts and describes a maintained standard identity-governance solution. IBM IGI is clearly the foundation, not claimed as its invention. A concrete maintained product built on vendor technology qualifies without requiring invention of every component.

rows.name: Trias Pharma
rows.reason: Recommend exclusion, pending main review: the service and tablet pages explicitly sell client CMC/formulation consultancy, CMO selection, on-site supervision and troubleshooting. Named cases are customer formulation projects; founder experience at prior employers is not a company-owned development platform. This is an affirmative scope recommendation, not a claim that formulation expertise lacks technical merit.
rows.currentReason: Withdraw the service-only exclusion: the specific medicinal-cannabis case says the company initiated development and successfully developed several stable marketed formulations. Original formulation/process development qualifies without patents or a standalone branded platform. The separate inhalation device remains a client collaboration, not credited as wholly Trias-owned.

rows.name: UMB
rows.reason: The newly read 2019 DevOps page describes a UMB-built provisioning solution on its cloud, but does not establish current continuation after the documented mesoneer separation. Remaining question: which original platform component is maintained by present-day UMB? Do not credit the divested identification/signature products to UMB or reject OSS-based development.

rows.name: Unimission
rows.reason: Recommend exclusion, pending main review: the detailed named offerings positively identify UniVision as SolarWinds-based and uNimbus as IBM Power/Green-hosted private-cloud operation with governance/support. These are vendor services, not attributable original products. The decision is grounded in the named catalogue, not vendor use alone or a missing patent.
rows.currentReason: Official company history explicitly states that development of Swiss Private Cloud uNimbus began in 2025. Green hosting, IBM infrastructure and SolarWinds-powered UniVision do not disprove original uNimbus development. The catalogue does not identify an original control-plane/software component or technical process. Prior exclusion is unsafe until this branch is resolved.

rows.name: Voviva
rows.reason: Dextra's case establishes genuine joint development of multilingual legal claims intake, still in development. Remaining question: does Voviva develop a common original system beyond this single client's workflow? Do not require commercial maturity or exclusive rights, but do not infer a reusable own product from a commissioned LLM integration.

rows.name: wetalkwithyou
rows.reason: Recommend exclusion, pending main review: the technology strategy and Ably case explicitly offer commissioned shops/web applications on established frameworks. This is affirmative generic agency delivery in the inspected catalogue, not a rule against open-source software or an assertion that hidden own technology cannot exist.

Remaining question: who develops that portal or another original control system? Access is resolved; operating the datacentre alone does not settle the specific software-development exception.
